items.title: What an ISMS Is and Why It Matters
items.summary: An ISMS is a systematic, risk-based management system for information security. This lesson explains what the system contains, why organisations build one, and how it differs from a mere control checklist.
objectives: Define an ISMS and its place inside enterprise governance
Explain why a compliance checklist alone is insufficient
Describe the relationship between an ISMS, an ISO 27001 certificate and a Statement of Applicability
Identify the key inputs a GRC professional must understand before leading an ISMS implementation

sections.heading: The problem with a checklist-only approach
sections.body: Most people who first encounter information security standards imagine a list of checkboxes: enable MFA, encrypt the laptops, train the staff, run the vulnerability scan, get the certificate. It is a seductive picture. Checkboxes are binary, testable and easy to audit. The problem is that security is not binary.
bullets: A checklist is static; an ISMS is a living system
Certification is evidence the system is running, not that the organisation is secure
Controls are chosen for organisations - there is no universal set
An ISMS must be embedded in the organisation's governance, not bolted on
sections.callout: An ISMS is a management system, not a checklist. Certification is evidence of a run system, not a guarantee of security.

sections.heading: Definitions that matter
sections.body: Before going further, a few terms need precision, because the vocabulary is used differently across ISO, NIST, ISACA and every regulator.
bullets: ISMS: the coherent management system for information security
ISO/IEC 27001: requirements for the management system; Annex A has the controls
ISO/IEC 27002: guidance on implementing those controls
Certification: third-party evidence that the system meets the standard's requirements
Statement of Applicability (SoA): maps the standard to your organisation

sections.heading: Where an ISMS sits in an enterprise
sections.body: An ISMS does not float free. It is part of the wider enterprise governance framework.
bullets: ISMS aligns with enterprise strategy, risk appetite and corporate policies
Connects to risk management, internal audit, management review and regulatory obligations
Isolated ISMS does not function as a management system
GRC professional manages the system, not just the certificate

sections.heading: The ISMS lifecycle in one picture
sections.body: The ISO/IEC 27001 implementation lifecycle is a continuous cycle, often drawn as a ring.
bullets: Context -> Leadership -> Planning -> Support -> Operate -> Improve
Risk assessment is a core clause (6.1), not optional
Continual improvement is a requirement, not a nice-to-have
table: Understanding of internal/external context, interested parties
Policy, roles, responsibilities, risk appetite alignment
Risk assessment, risk treatment plan, SoA
Competence, awareness, documented information, operational controls
Operational controls, monitoring, internal audit, management review
ISMS documentation, risk register, SoA, audit reports, review minutes

practicalExercise.title: Write an ISMS scope and context statement
practicalExercise.brief: Write a scope and context statement for a hypothetical ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS for a fictional company.
steps: Write a one-paragraph context paragraph: what the company does, what information it holds, why security matters
List the interested parties and their expectations
practicalExercise.deliverable: A written scope and context statement.
evaluationCriteria: Context paragraph connects the risks to business drivers, not just technical risks
Are the interested parties credible and appropriately differentiated?

references: ISO/IEC 27006-1: requirements for bodies providing audit and certification of ISMS

items.title: Leadership, Policy and Roles
items.summary: Clauses 4 to 7 of ISO/IEC 27001 establish who owns the ISMS and what they must do. This lesson covers leadership commitment, the information security policy, roles and responsibilities, and the planning process.
objectives: Explain the leadership requirements of ISO/IEC 27001 clauses 5, 6 and 7
Write a workable information security policy
Assign roles and responsibilities for ISMS ownership
Understand how the ISMS connects to enterprise governance

sections.heading: Leadership is the foundation
sections.body: ISO/IEC 27001 places the responsibility for the ISMS squarely on leadership. Clause 5.1 requires top management to demonstrate leadership and commitment. What does that mean in practice?
bullets: Top management must agree the ISMS objectives
Leaders must communicate the importance of the ISMS
Leaders must ensure resources are available
Leaders must review ISMS performance
sections.callout: Leadership commitment is not a formality. Without stated and visible leadership, an ISMS will not function.

sections.heading: The information security policy
sections.body: Clause 5.2 requires an information security policy. This is not a lengthy document. It is a short statement of intent that sets the direction for the ISMS.
bullets: Policy must be approved by top management
Policy must be communicated to all employees
Policy must be reviewed at planned intervals
Policy must be available to interested parties who need it
table: To protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information
All information assets of the organisation
All staff must follow the policy and escalate concerns

sections.heading: Roles and responsibilities
sections.body: Clause 5.3 requires the organisation to determine and assign roles and responsibilities. In a GRC context, this means clarity on who does what.
bullets: ISMS sponsor: typically the CEO or board representative
ISMS owner: typically the CISO or head of security
ISMS project lead: typically the GRC manager or security lead
Control owners: department heads accountable for their controls
Internal audit: independent assessment of the ISMS
table: Authority and resources for the ISMS

practicalExercise.title: Draft an information security policy
practicalExercise.brief: Draft a short information security policy for a fictional company. It should state the purpose, scope, commitment and review frequency. Include the approving authority.
steps: Write a policy statement (no more than 500 words)
Choose the approving authority
Identify who will review the policy and how often
practicalExercise.deliverable: A written policy draft with approval block.
evaluationCriteria: Policy covers purpose, scope, commitment and review
Policy is suitable for communication to all staff

items.title: Risk Assessment and Treatment
items.summary: Clause 6 of ISO/IEC 27001 is all about planning for risk. This lesson covers risk assessment, risk treatment, the Statement of Applicability, and the link between the risk register and the control programme.
objectives: Explain risk assessment and risk treatment as separate activities
Write a risk assessment methodology suitable for a small organisation
Build a Statement of Applicability from an organisation's risk register
Explain why the SoA is an output of risk treatment, not a starting point

sections.heading: Risk assessment: the starting point
sections.body: ISO/IEC 27001 clause 6.1 requires the organisation to plan its actions to address the risks to information security.
bullets: Risk identification: what could go wrong
Risk analysis: how bad and how likely
Risk evaluation: is the risk acceptable
sections.callout: Risk assessment is the input to control selection. Controls are not selected first and risks second.

sections.heading: The risk assessment methodology
sections.body: A risk assessment methodology is the structured process your organisation uses to assess risk.
bullets: Identify assets: what are you protecting?
Identify threats: what could harm those assets?
Identify vulnerabilities: what weaknesses could be exploited?
Calculate likelihood and impact
Determine the risk rating
Compare against risk appetite
Record the result

sections.heading: Risk treatment
sections.body: Once risks are assessed, the organisation must decide what to do about them.
bullets: Accept: the risk is within risk appetite
Treat: apply controls to reduce the risk
Avoid: change the plan to remove the risk
Transfer: share the risk with another party
Escalate: refer to a higher level of management
table: Low risk, low impact - accept and monitor
Do not store credit card data on-premises

sections.heading: The Statement of Applicability
sections.body: The Statement of Applicability (SoA) is the bridge between the standard and the organisation.
bullets: The SoA is the output of risk treatment
Non-selected controls must be explained
The SoA is reviewed annually and on change
The SoA is the basis of the certification audit

sections.heading: How the GRC professional uses these tools
sections.body: The GRC professional's skills in the risk management process.
bullets: Risk appetite statement: the threshold against which risks are judged
SoA maintenance: the living document representing current practice
Integration with enterprise risk: the ISMS risk register must not be a silo
Evidence: every selection or exclusion must be justifiable

sections.heading: Practical exercise
sections.body: Identify five risks for a fictional organisation and decide on a treatment for each.
bullets: Customer data breach: likelihood 4, impact 5, treat
Key staff leaving: likelihood 3, impact 4, accept
Ransomware attack: likelihood 5, impact 5, treat heavily
Third-party failure: likelihood 3, impact 6, escalate

practicalExercise.title: Build a risk treatment plan
practicalExercise.brief: Write a short risk treatment plan for a fictional company. Identify 5 risks, score each, decide the treatment, and record the rationale.
steps: Identify 5 business-relevant risks
Score each using a 5x5 matrix
Decide treatment for each
Write the rationale for each decision
evaluationCriteria: Risks are business-relevant, not just technical
Treatments are appropriate to the risk rating

items.title: Annex A Control Architecture
items.summary: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A contains 93 controls. This lesson explains the control architecture and how to use it in practice.
objectives: List the four Annex A control categories and their counts
Explain the difference between organisational, people, physical and technological controls
Select controls appropriate to an organisation's risk assessment
Describe how controls are audited

sections.heading: The Annex A control catalogue
sections.body: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A contains 93 controls. They are not mandatory - they are a catalogue from which you select.
bullets: The controls are grouped into 4 categories
Category A.5: Organisational controls
Category A.6: People controls
Category A.7: Physical controls
Category A.8: Technological controls

sections.heading: Organisational controls (A.5): 37 controls
sections.body: Organisational controls are the policies, processes and governance arrangements.
bullets: Information security policies
Organisational change management
Asset management
Access control policies
Cryptography policy
Physical security policy
Supplier relationships
Incident management policy
Business continuity
Compliance and legal requirements

sections.heading: People controls (A.6): 8 controls
sections.body: People controls cover the human element of information security.
bullets: Background checks
Terms of employment
Security awareness training
Disciplinary process
Confidentiality agreements
IT equipment handling
Removal of access when leaving
Confidential information handling

sections.heading: Physical controls (A.7): 14 controls
sections.body: Physical controls protect the physical environment.
bullets: Data centre security
Physical entry controls
Physical security monitoring
Clear desk and clear screen
Equipment security
Cabling security
Storage media controls
Secure disposal
Shops and offices
Transportation
Visitor management
Working in secure areas
Protection against electrical power disturbances
Fire protection

sections.heading: Technological controls (A.8): 34 controls
sections.body: Technological controls are the technical defences against security incidents.
bullets: Access security
Identity management
Access rights
User devices
Mobile devices
Remote working
Encryption
Public key infrastructure
System acquisition
System development
System operation
Incident management
Business continuity
Cameras for visual surveillance
Logging and monitoring
Clock synchronization
Privacy and protection of PII
Legal requirements for evidence
Malicious software detection
Data leakage prevention
Network security
Network services
Web filtering
Use of cryptography
Secure coding
External system components
Information backup
Redundancy
Resilience of processing facilities
Threat intelligence
Vulnerability management

sections.heading: How to use the control catalogue in practice
sections.body: The control catalogue is a tool, not a target. It is used in five steps.
bullets: Step 1: Understand your context and risks
Step 2: Identify which controls apply
Step 3: Document the selection in the SoA
Step 4: Implement the selected controls
Step 5: Audit to verify they work

sections.heading: Annex A in audit testing
sections.body: When auditing an ISMS, the auditor checks that controls are selected, implemented, and effective.
bullets: Audit sampling: check a sample of controls for effectiveness
Interview control owners
Review evidence of control operation
Check the SoA is current

practicalExercise.title: Select controls from Annex A
practicalExercise.brief: Choose a fictional organisation. Identify 10 controls from Annex A you would select and 3 you would exclude. Explain each selection or exclusion.
steps: Identify the organisation's context and risks
Select at least 10 controls from Annex A
Exclude 3 controls with reasons
Document in a SoA table
practicalExercise.deliverable: A Statement of Applicability table with selections and exclusions documented.
evaluationCriteria: Selections are appropriate to the organisation's context
The SoA table is clear and auditable

items.title: Recording Information and Operational Controls
items.summary: Clauses 7 and 8 of ISO/IEC 27001 cover competence, awareness, documented information, operational controls and monitoring. This lesson covers how the ISMS is run day to day.
objectives: Explain the document control and operational control requirements of ISO/IEC 27001
Write a document control procedure suitable for a small organisation
Describe how operational controls are monitored and verified
Explain the relationship between monitoring and measurement and management review

sections.heading: Documented information
sections.body: ISO/IEC 27001 makes extensive use of documented information. Documentation is not a bureaucracy, it is the organisation's memory.
bullets: Do: identify what documents you need
Do: control their creation, approval and review
Don't: write documents nobody reads
Don't: lose documents when people leave
Do: make sure the right people can find the right documents

sections.heading: Competence and awareness
sections.body: ISO/IEC 27001 requires the organisation to ensure people are competent and aware of their information security responsibilities.
bullets: Competence: having the right skills (hired or trained)
Awareness: knowing how to apply those skills
Training: planned and delivered
Assessment: proving the training worked
Awareness: repeating the message to keep it relevant

sections.heading: Operational controls in practice
sections.body: Operational controls are the things that happen day to day in the organisation to keep security working.
bullets: Change management: changes to systems are assessed and approved
Privileged access: limited and monitored
Vulnerability management: identified and patched
Incident management: detected, assessed, and responded to
Asset management: assets are tracked and protected
Backup and recovery: data can be recovered

sections.heading: Monitoring and measurement
sections.body: You cannot improve what you do not measure. ISO/IEC 27001 requires the organisation to monitor and measure its ISMS.
bullets: Define what you will measure
Collect the data objectively
Analyse the data
Act on the findings
Report the findings to management
sections.callout: Measurement without action is vanity. Every metric you collect should drive a decision or a conversation.

sections.heading: Internal audit
sections.body: Clause 9.2 requires internal audit of the ISMS. This is independent assurance that the system is working.
bullets: The audit is independent of the area audited
The audit plan is based on risk
The audit findings are recorded
Corrective actions are tracked to completion
The audit programme is reviewed annually

sections.heading: Practical exercise
sections.body: Write a short monitoring and measurement plan for a fictional organisation. Identify 5 metrics, how they will be measured, and who will review them.
bullets: Metric: number of security incidents per quarter
Metric: audit findings closed within 30 days
Metric: % of employees completing training
Metric: mean time to respond to incidents

practicalExercise.title: Write a monitoring and measurement plan
practicalExercise.brief: Write a short monitoring and measurement plan for a fictional company. Identify 5 metrics, how they will be measured, and who will review them.
steps: Identify 5 metrics that matter to your organisation
Describe how each metric will be measured
Identify who will review the metric and how often
practicalExercise.deliverable: A short monitoring and measurement plan document.

items.title: Inner Audit, Management Review and Improvement
items.summary: Clauses 9 and 10 of ISO/IEC 27001 complete the ISMS lifecycle. This lesson covers internal audit, management review, nonconformity, corrective action and continual improvement.
objectives: Explain the purpose of internal audit in the ISMS lifecycle
Describe how to run a management review meeting
Distinguish nonconformity from a finding, and corrective action from recurrence prevention
Explain what continual improvement means in practice

sections.heading: The ISMS is never finished
sections.body: ISO/IEC 27001 Clause 10 requires continual improvement. This is the finish line that keeps moving. An ISMS is not a project to be completed; it is a system to be improved.
bullets: Continual improvement: a never-ending cycle of getting better
Nonconformity: when something does not meet the requirement
Corrective action: fixing the problem and preventing it from recurring
Improvement: making the system better than it was before

sections.heading: Internal audit
sections.body: Internal audit is the independent check that the ISMS is working as intended. It is not a punishment exercise; it is how the organisation learns.
bullets: Internal audit is independent: the auditor is not responsible for the area being audited
The audit plan is based on risk
The audit is conducted to the standard
Audit results are reported to management
Corrective actions are tracked to closure

sections.heading: Nonconformity and corrective action
sections.body: The audit finds nonconformities - places where the ISMS does not meet the requirement. Corrective action addresses them.
bullets: Nonconformity: failure to meet a requirement
Cause: why did this happen?
Corrective action: what will we do about it?
Effectiveness: has the corrective action worked?
Closure: the action is complete
table: A control is not working as required
Next audit shows passwords rotated on time

sections.heading: Management review
sections.body: Clause 9.3 requires top management to review the ISMS at planned intervals. This is where the ISMS meets the board.
bullets: Management review is planned, not ad hoc
Review inputs: audit results, status of corrective actions, changes in context
Review outputs: changes to the ISMS, resource needs, improvement opportunities
The review is minuted and the minutes are retained
table: Findings from the last internal audit
Determine if the ISMS scope needs to change

sections.heading: Putting it all together
sections.body: The ISMS is one continuous cycle: context -> leadership -> planning -> support -> operate -> improve -> back to context.
bullets: Plan: risk assessment and treatment
Act: controls implemented
Check: monitoring, internal audit
Act: management review and improvement

sections.heading: Practical exercise
sections.body: You are the GRC manager of a fictional company. The internal audit has found three nonconformities. Write a corrective action plan for each.
bullets: NC1: No asset register - corrective action: implement asset register within 30 days
NC2: Backup failures - corrective action: investigate and fix within 14 days
NC3: No documented risk assessment - corrective action: complete within 60 days

practicalExercise.title: Write a corrective action plan
practicalExercise.brief: You are the GRC manager. The internal audit has found three nonconformities. Write a corrective action plan for each.
steps: Identify the nonconformity
Find the root cause
Write the corrective action
Identify the owner and deadline
Define how you will verify effectiveness
evaluationCriteria: Root cause is identified, not just the symptom

items.title: Certification Readiness and the Audit Process
items.summary: Once the ISMS is running, the organisation must pass the certification audit. This lesson explains the audit process, what the certification body tests, and how to prepare.
objectives: Explain the difference between Stage 1 and Stage 2 certification audits
Describe what a certification body will test during the audit
Prepare an audit-ready ISMS with evidence organised
Explain how to use audit findings to drive continuous improvement

sections.heading: The certification journey
sections.body: ISO/IEC 27001 certification is a process, not a moment. The organisation goes through several stages before receiving its certificate.
bullets: Stage 1: The certification body checks the ISMS is designed correctly
Stage 2: The certification body checks the ISMS actually works
Surveillance audits: periodic checks to maintain certification
Recertification: renewal at the end of the certification period

sections.heading: What the certification body tests
sections.body: During the audit, the certification body will test that the ISMS meets the requirements of ISO/IEC 27001.
bullets: The ISMS is aligned with the standard's clauses
The Statement of Applicability is complete
Controls are implemented and effective
Internal audit and management review have occurred
The management system is working in practice

sections.heading: Preparing for the audit
sections.body: Audit preparation is a continuous activity, not a sprint before the audit date.
bullets: Keep documents up to date: the SoA, policies, procedures
Track corrective actions: ensure they are completed
Evidence: files are organised and retrievable
Interviews: control owners are prepared to explain
The SMIS: a single source of truth for all documents

sections.heading: The auditor's approach
sections.body: The auditor will use a mix of evidence review and interviews to form an opinion.
bullets: Document review: checking the SoA, policies and procedures
Interviews: talking to control owners and staff
Observation: seeing controls in operation
Evidence review: checking records of control operation

sections.heading: Handling audit findings
sections.body: When the audit finds issues, the response determines how the certification proceeds.
bullets: Minor nonconformity: a small gap, corrected and evidenced
Major nonconformity: a significant gap
Opportunity for improvement: not a failure, but room to improve
Full certification: if major nonconformities are corrected

sections.heading: Practical exercise
sections.body: You are preparing for a Stage 2 certification audit. Write a pre-audit checklist and evidence preparation plan.
bullets: Check the SoA is current
Organise evidence files
Prepare control owners for interviews
Run a mock audit
Validate corrective actions are complete

practicalExercise.title: Prepare an audit-ready evidence pack
practicalExercise.brief: Write a pre-audit checklist for a fictional company preparing for a Stage 2 ISO 27001 certification audit.
steps: List the documents you would need to have available
Describe the evidence preparation process
Create a mock interview plan for control owners

items.title: Capstone Project: ISMS Implementation for a Virtual Company
items.summary: This lesson brings together all the lessons from Module 2 into a capstone project. You will implement an ISMS for a fictional organisation.
objectives: Integrate the knowledge from Module 2 into a practical ISMS implementation
Produce a scope, context statement, risk assessment, SoA and implementation plan
Demonstrate understanding of the ISMS lifecycle and continual improvement

sections.heading: The capstone project
sections.body: This capstone project brings together everything from this module. You will implement an ISMS for a fictional organisation.
bullets: Part 1: Scope and context
Part 2: Risk assessment
Part 3: Statement of Applicability
Part 4: Implementation plan

sections.heading: Project scope
sections.body: The fictional company is GreenLeaf Health, a regional medical-supply distributor with 250 employees, a warehouse, and a customer database of 8,000 patient records. They handle email, an intranet, and a customer portal.
bullets: Assets: patient records, financial data, operational systems
Risks: data breach, system failure, staff error, supplier failure
Regulatory: GDPR, HIPAA

sections.heading: Part 1: Scope and context
sections.body: Write the scope and context statement. Include the interested parties and the key risk factors.
bullets: Context: what the company does and why security matters
Interested parties: patients, regulators, staff, insurers

sections.heading: Part 2: Risk assessment
sections.body: Follow the methodology from Lesson 3. Identify at least 5 risks, score them, and decide on treatment.
bullets: Risk 1: Patient data breach - High, treat with controls
Risk 2: Ransomware - Extreme, treat heavily
Risk 3: Staff leaving with customer data - High, treat

sections.heading: Part 3: Statement of Applicability
sections.body: Create a SoA table with at least 10 selected controls and 3 excluded controls with reasons.
bullets: Selected: A.5.7 (data classification), A.5.12 (access control), A.6.1.3 (training), A.8.13 (backup), A.8.10 (encryption)

sections.heading: Part 4: Implementation plan
sections.body: Create a 90-day implementation plan with milestones and deliverables.
bullets: Month 1: Policies and project setup
Month 2: Controls implemented
Month 3: Internal audit and management review

practicalExercise.title: ISMS Implementation Capstone
practicalExercise.brief: Implement an ISMS for the fictional company GreenLeaf Health. Deliver: scope and context statement, risk assessment, SoA, and 90-day implementation plan.
steps: Write the scope and context statement
Conduct a risk assessment
Create the SoA
Plan the 90-day implementation
evaluationCriteria: All four parts are complete and interconnected
Scope, risk assessment and controls align
The submission demonstrates understanding of the ISMS lifecycle
